Little Timmy was a villager who first appeared in Warcraft III: Reign of Chaos. He was a young boy and son of Alicia. He lived in a farmhouse in a village between the Silver Hand encampment and Strahnbrad at the beginning of the Third War. While Strahnbrad was under attack by the Blackrock clan, Little Timmy was kidnapped by a pack of gnolls. Prince Arthas rescued Timmy at the behest of his mother. Little Timmy makes another appearance in Warcraft III: The Frozen Throne as a vendor selling Ice Shards. Little Timmy appeared again in Warcraft III: The Frozen Throne. The Living Leggings are a pair of crafted leather pants, obviously with mid-50's druids in mind. They are crafted by Elemental Leatherworkers, the pattern requires skill 285/300, and drops off Deadwood Shamans in Felwood. They match quite well with the Living Breastplate and Living Shoulders, also crafted by an Elemental Leatherworker. Though these items bear similar names, and are obviously designed with the same general texture appearance, they are not a real set and provide no set bonus.

Liu Lang was a prominent pandaren scholar and explorer, the first of his people to leave Pandaria in the years following the Sundering. His legacy is celebrated by the pandaren in both the Wanderer's Festival and Spirit Festival.

Little Lu guided Rell and Sully across the forests, having found Amber, inspecting the Serpent's Spine, visiting the Lair of the Jade Witch and investigating the Grookin Hill, he returned home. He was considered to be a part of SI:7 by its agents. Some time later, Lu accompanied Amber to the newly retaken Slingtail Pits.

Little Black Rams are rams found in Loch Modan. They are only present during daytime.

The Lion of the Waves is an Alliance ship that assaulted Bladefist Bay shortly after the destruction of Theramore. It was captained by Captain Telda Stonefist and served as King Varian Wrynn's flagship but was sunk by Horde ships during the naval battle.

Liu Lang's Final Rest marks the resting place of Liu Lang, the first pandaren explorer, in the Wood of Staves on the Wandering Isle. This is where Liu Lang planted his umbrella after saying farewell to his old friend, Shen-zin Su, upon whose back the Isle sits. He likely traveled to that particular spot because it also happens to be the closest point of the land where one can be near and see the head of Shen-zin Su.

Lion's Watch Engineers are gnomes located at Lion's Watch in Tanaan Jungle. They are part of the Alliance offensive against Gul'dan's Iron Horde in Tanaan. They build and maintain the vehicles and siege weapons and can be found throughout Lion's Watch doing so.

Lion's Watch Paladins are draenei located in Lion's Watch in Tanaan Jungle. They are part of the Hand of the Prophet and also the Alliance offensive against 's Iron Horde in Tanaan. They guard Lion's Watch and can be found throughout it.

Lion's Watch Riflemen are dwarves located at Lion's Watch in Tanaan Jungle. They are involved in the Alliance offensive against Gul'dan's Iron Horde in Tanaan. They are stationed atop the tower in Lion's Watch. Some of them can be seen patrolling the edge while several others are seen resting. Two can be seen playing a game of Hearthstone, and will often utter quotes and phrases that reference various Hearthstone inside jokes.

Lion's Watch Footmen are humans located at Lion's Watch in Tanaan Jungle. They are involved in the Alliance offensive against Gul'dan's Iron Horde in Tanaan. They can be found guarding the outside walls of Lion's Watch, while Lion's Watch Paladins guard the inside. Several can be seen mounted on horses and patrolling the area in and around Lion's Watch.
